newsitem.title: USA: U.S., China approve Hong Kong port call deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S., China approve Hong Kong port call deal.

text.p: The U.S. and Chinese foreign ministers gave final approval on Monday to an agreement allowing U.S. port calls in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to Beijing's control on July 1, the State Department said.
But spokesman Nicholas Burns announced no other concrete results from a two-hour meeting between Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen.

"Based on the expert level talks and based on their discussions today, we have reached an agreement governing procedures requests and approvals for continuation of United States Navy port calls to Hong Kong after July 1," Burns told reporters.

He said in December, the Chinese defence minister reached an agreement in principle with his U.S. counterpart to continue port calls after reversion but there was at that time no specific understanding of how those port call decisions would come about.

But Burns, who briefed reporters after the Qian-Albright meeting, announced no other specific achievements. He said Albright had urged China to take concrete steps on a number of rucial issues, such as preserving Hong Kong's autonomy and freedoms after July 1, imporving human rights and establishing a nationwide weapons export control system.
The two ministers were later to have a two-hour working dinner.
